mainTopic: When a ברכה on wine must be repeated after bentching, and how רבא performed הבדלה (a torch, and the number of distinctions).
overview: This amud finishes a story about the תלמידי רב at a meal. They first said 'Give us a cup so we can bentch,' then changed their minds and wanted to keep drinking. רב ייבא סבא told them in the name of רב that the earlier ברכה on wine no longer counts, because they had taken their minds off drinking (היסח הדעת). Next, אמימר, מר זוטרא and רב אשי each make ברכות on wine differently at one meal, and רב אחא בר רבא asks whom to follow. אמימר says he kept changing his mind, and מר זוטרא says he follows the תלמידי רב. רב אשי says the הלכה is not like them and tries to prove it from רב's order of יקנ"ה. The גמרא rejects that proof: bentching shows a person has finished drinking, while קידוש does not. The amud then returns to the visit of רב יעקב בר אבא at רבא's house. There we learn that a torch is the best way to do הבדלה, and that the הבדלה blessing should list between three and seven distinctions. The guest's reply to that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The students change their minds about bentching
steps.stepSummary: רב ייבא סבא is serving the תלמידי רב. They first ask for a cup to bentch on, then change their minds and ask for a cup to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ייבא סבא stood over them to serve them. They said to him: 'Give us a cup and we will bentch.' In the end they said to him: 'Give us a cup and we will drink.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a story that began earlier, setting up the case for רב's ruling in the next step. The diners announce they are ready to bentch, then decide to keep drinking instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that they actually said out loud 'let us bentch.' That statement shows they had mentally ended the meal and the drinking. The question is whether they can now drink without a new ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: stood over them, meaning served them at the meal
and we will bentch (say ברכת המזון)

steps.confusionAlert: The diners here are the תלמידי רב (the students of רב), who were introduced on the previous amud. מר זוטרא refers back to them later here.

phrases.english: Rav Yeiva the Elder stood over them (serving them).
phrases.notes: The 'them' are the students of רב, mentioned on the previous amud.

phrases.english: They said to him: Give us a cup and we will recite Grace after Meals.

phrases.aramaic: לְסוֹף אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הַב לַן וְנִישְׁתֵּי,
phrases.english: In the end they said to him: Give us a cup and we will drink,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the תלמידי רב begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the case: the diners declared they would bentch, then wanted to drink more.

steps.title: רב's ruling that they may no longer drink
steps.stepSummary: רב ייבא סבא quotes רב: once you said 'let us bentch,' you are forbidden to drink without a new ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: This is what רב said: Since you said 'Give us a cup and we will bentch,' you are now forbidden to drink.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ייבא סבא gives a ruling from רב: announcing that you are about to bentch cuts off your right to keep drinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Forbidden to drink' does not mean drinking is banned. It means the earlier ברכה on wine no longer covers more drinking, so drinking without a new ברכה would be forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: it has become forbidden to you

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean they may not drink at all. They simply need a fresh בורא פרי הגפן first.

phrases.english: He said to them: Thus said Rav:
Since you said 'Give us and we will bless,'
it has become forbidden for you to drink.
phrases.notes: That is, without a new blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the case set up in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once a person declares he is about to bentch, his earlier ברכה on wine no longer covers further drinking.

steps.title: Asking for the reason
steps.stepSummary: רב ייבא סבא, still speaking to the diners, asks why saying 'let us bentch' should stop them from drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ייבא סבא himself asks for the logic behind רב's ruling, setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing was eaten or drunk in between, so it is not obvious why mere words should matter. The question asks what principle makes the statement count as a break.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why saying 'let us bentch' makes further drinking forbidden without a new ברכה.

steps.title: Because they took their minds off drinking
steps.stepSummary: The reason is היסח הדעת: by planning to bentch, they mentally ended their drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because you diverted your minds from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ייבא סבא explains to the diners that once they planned to bentch, they stopped thinking about drinking. So the old ברכה is over.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברכה covers what a person intends to eat or drink. Once he consciously decides he is finished, the ברכה's coverage ends. Any new drinking needs a new ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: you took your minds off it
mental diversion; deciding you are done

steps.whatToRemember: רב's rule: saying 'let us bentch' counts as היסח הדעת from drinking. After that, a new ברכה on wine is required.
steps.whyThisMatters: היסח הדעת is the basic concept behind the rest of this passage. אמימר and מר זוטרא both explain their practice in terms of it.

phrases.english: Because you diverted your attention.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Declaring an intent to bentch is היסח הדעת, which ends the coverage of the ברכה on wine.

steps.title: Three sages bless on wine in three different ways
steps.stepSummary: At one meal, אמימר blessed on every cup, מר זוטרא on the first and last cups, and רב אשי only on the first cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר, מר זוטרא and רב אשי were sitting at a meal, and רב אחא son of רבא was serving them. אמימר blessed on every single cup. מר זוטרא blessed on the first cup and on the last cup. רב אשי blessed on the first cup and did not bless again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story that shows three different practices for ברכות on wine at a meal. It sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'last cup' for מר זוטרא is the cup after ברכת המזון. So he treats bentching as a break. רב אשי treats nothing as a break, and אמימר seems to treat every cup as new.

phrases.english: Ameimar, Mar Zutra, and Rav Ashi
were sitting at a meal,

phrases.aramaic: וְקָאֵי עֲלַיְיהוּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא.
phrases.english: and Rav Acha son of Rava stood over them (serving).

phrases.aramaic: אַמֵּימָר בָּרֵיךְ עַל כׇּל כָּסָא וְכָסָא,
phrases.english: Ameimar blessed over each and every cup,
and Mar Zutra blessed over the first cup
and over the last cup,
Rav Ashi blessed over the first cup,
and did not bless any more.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר וּמָר זוּטְרָא וְרַב אָשֵׁי הֲווֹ יָתְבִי בִּסְעוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the same topic of when a ברכה on wine must be repeated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three practices are recorded: blessing on every cup, blessing on the first and last cups, or blessing on the first cup only.

steps.title: רב אחא asks whose practice to follow
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר רבא asks the three sages which of them people should follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר רבא said to them: According to whom should we act?
steps.whatsHappening: Having seen three different practices, the server asks which one is correct. This sets up each sage's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question forces each sage to explain whether his practice reflects a general rule or something specific to that meal.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב אַחָא בַּר רָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Rava said to them:
We, according to whom should we act?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the three practices described in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three practices is the correct הלכה.

steps.title: אמימר: I kept changing my mind
steps.stepSummary: אמימר explains that he blessed every time because he kept deciding to stop drinking and then changed his mind.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר says his practice was not a general rule. Each cup he meant to be his last, so each new cup needed a new ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His behavior is an application of היסח הדעת, not a disagreement with the others. Someone who plans to keep drinking would not need to bless on every cup.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude from אמימר that one must bless on every cup. He blessed each time only because he kept deciding to stop.

phrases.english: Ameimar said: I reconsidered (each time).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to רב אחא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His blessing on every cup came from his personal היסח הדעת each time, not from a general rule.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: I follow the students of רב
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא says he follows the תלמידי רב, who treat bentching as a break that requires a new ברכה on wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: I acted like the students of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא explains his blessing on the last cup. He holds that ברכת המזון ends the earlier ברכה on wine, just as in the earlier story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties back to steps 1-4. Preparing to bentch is היסח הדעת, so the cup after bentching needs its own ברכה.

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
I acted in accordance with the students of Rav.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second answer to רב אחא's question. It connects back to the story in steps 1-4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Bentching is a break in drinking, so the cup after ברכת המזון needs a new ברכה.

steps.title: רב אשי: the הלכה does not follow the students of רב
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי rules that the הלכה is not like the תלמידי רב, so bentching does not require a new ברכה on wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב אשי said: The הלכה is not like the students of רב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי explains his own practice of blessing only once by rejecting מר זוטרא's source. His proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב אשי's view, ברכת המזון is not a break that ends the ברכה on wine. That is why he never repeated it.

phrases.english: And Rav Ashi said:
The halacha is not in accordance with the students of Rav,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third answer to רב אחא's question in step 6. It rejects the position מר זוטרא just relied on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The view of the תלמידי רב that bentching is a break requiring a new ברכה on wine.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It conflicts with רב's own ruling, which is shown in the next step.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The הלכה is not like the תלמידי רב, so ברכת המזון is not a break, and the first ברכה on wine also covers the cup after bentching.

steps.title: Proof from רב's rule of יקנ"ה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי proves his point from רב's order for יום טוב after שבת: wine, קידוש, candle, הבדלה. The single ברכה on wine covers הבדלה even though קידוש comes in between.
steps.simpleTranslation: For when a יום טוב falls after שבת, רב said the order is יקנ"ה (יין, קידוש, נר, הבדלה).
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings proof from רב himself. A long interruption such as קידוש does not require a new ברכה on wine, so bentching should not either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יקנ"ה there is one ברכה on wine at the start, and it still counts for הבדלה afterward. That shows a ברכה or interruption in the middle does not cancel the ברכה on wine. By the same logic, ברכת המזון does not cancel it.

keyTerms.term: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת
keyTerms.meaning: a יום טוב that falls right after שבת (מוצאי שבת)
יין, קידוש, נר, הבדלה: the order of ברכות on that night

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: bentching is not a break in drinking, so one ברכה on wine is enough. He tries to prove it from רב's rule of יקנ"ה, where קידוש does not interrupt between the wine and הבדלה. The next step rejects this proof.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not arguing with רב. He argues that רב's own ruling of יקנ"ה goes against the view of the students. The גמרא then rejects this argument in the next step.
steps.whyThisMatters: יקנ"ה is the order still used today when יום טוב falls on מוצאי שבת. Here it serves as a proof about interruptions after a ברכה on wine.

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת,
phrases.english: for regarding a Festival that falls after Shabbat,
Rav said: YaKNeH (wine, kiddush, candle, havdalah).
phrases.notes: There is only one blessing on wine, even though קידוש separates it from הבדלה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for רב אשי's rejection in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That ברכת המזון is not a break requiring a new ברכה on wine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling of יקנ"ה: one ברכה on wine covers הבדלה even though קידוש comes in between.

steps.title: Bentching ends the drinking, but קידוש does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב אשי's proof. Bentching shows that a person has decided to stop drinking. קידוש in the middle of the wine does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that is not so. There, he took his mind off drinking. Here, he did not take his mind off drinking.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that רב אשי's proof from the יום טוב order does not work. The two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי compared bentching to קידוש coming between the wine and הבדלה. The גמרא points out a key difference. When a person gets ready to bentch, he has stopped thinking about drinking, so it is a real break. When he says קידוש, he is still planning to drink, so the first ברכה on the wine still covers what comes later.

keyTerms.meaning: That is not so (the גמרא rejects the argument)
He took his mind off it (lit. uprooted his mind)

steps.whatToRemember: What matters is the person's mind. Bentching means he has finished drinking, so it counts as a break. קידוש does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes רב אשי's proof. It also explains the view of the תלמידי רב, who say a new ברכה on wine is needed after bentching.

phrases.english: And that is not so.
There, he took his mind off drinking.
Here, he did not take his mind off drinking.
phrases.notes: "Here" means קידוש and הבדלה on יום טוב after שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רב אשי's proof is rejected. His ruling is not directly overturned.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The cases do not match. Bentching means the person has stopped drinking. קידוש does not.

steps.title: Why light a torch when a candle is already burning?
steps.stepSummary: Back in the story, רבא's attendant lights a torch for הבדלה. רב יעקב בר אבא asks why this is needed when a candle is already there.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it was time for הבדלה, the attendant got up and lit a torch from a candle. רב יעקב בר אבא said to רבא: Why do you need all this? There is a candle right here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of רב יעקב בר אבא at רבא's house. The guest challenges the extra effort of lighting a torch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guest thinks the candle that was already burning is good enough for the ברכה on fire. Lighting a separate torch looks like needless extra effort.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do you need all this?

steps.confusionAlert: Each "אמר ליה" in this story is a conversation between רב יעקב בר אבא and רבא. The guest is talking to רבא, not to the attendant.

phrases.english: When the time came to make havdala,
his attendant got up and lit a torch from a candle.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְמָה לָךְ כּוּלֵּי הַאי,
phrases.english: He (Rav Yaakov bar Abba) said to him: Why do you need all this?
The candle is right here!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back from the side discussion to the main story of the visit.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of a separate torch for הבדלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A candle was already burning, so the torch seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רבא says the attendant did it on his own
steps.stepSummary: רבא first answers that the attendant acted on his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: The attendant did it on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers by saying he did not tell the attendant to light the torch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer does not defend the torch at all. It only says the torch was not רבא's instruction.

phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him: The attendant, on his own,
did this by himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question about the torch.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא did not order the torch. The attendant decided on his own.

steps.title: The attendant must have learned it from you
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב בר אבא rejects this. The attendant would only do this if he had heard it from רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If he had not heard it from you, he would not have done it!
steps.whatsHappening: The guest does not accept רבא's answer and pushes him to explain the torch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An attendant copies what his master teaches. So the torch must come from רבא's own view, and רבא still has to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master (a polite way to say "you")

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ
phrases.english: He said to him: If he had not heard it
from the Master, he would not have done it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָא שְׁמִיעַ לֵיהּ מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר, לָא הֲוָה עָבֵיד
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבא had nothing to do with the torch.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Attendants act based on what their master teaches.

steps.title: A torch is the best way to do הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that using a torch for הבדלה is the best way to do the מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Doesn't the Master hold that a torch for הבדלה is the best way to do the מצוה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא now gives the real reason for the torch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A single candle is enough, but a torch is better. The ברכה is בורא מאורי האש ("who creates the lights of fire"), and a torch with many flames gives more light. That is why the attendant lit one.

keyTerms.meaning: The best way to do a מצוה
The ceremony that separates שבת from the weekday

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the custom of using a braided הבדלה candle with several wicks.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לֵיהּ מָר
phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him: Does the Master not hold
that a torch for havdala is the best way to do the מצוה?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָבַר לֵיהּ מָר אֲבוּקָה לְהַבְדָּלָה מִצְוָה מִן הַמּוּבְחָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real answer to the torch question after step 14 pushed back.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A torch is the best way to do the מצוה of fire in הבדלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A torch is the מצוה מן המובחר for the fire in הבדלה, so lighting it is not needless effort even though a candle was present.

steps.title: רבא says four distinctions in הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the ברכה of הבדלה with a list of four distinctions.
steps.simpleTranslation: He began and said: "Who separates between holy and ordinary, between light and darkness, between Israel and the nations, between the seventh day and the six days of work."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא records the wording רבא used for הבדלה. This sets up the guest's next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא lists four separate distinctions in the ברכה. The next step will ask why he needs more than one.

keyTerms.meaning: Who separates between holy and ordinary

phrases.english: He began and said:
"Who separates between holy and ordinary,
between light and darkness,
between Israel and the nations,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי לְשֵׁשֶׁת יְמֵי הַמַּעֲשֶׂה״
phrases.english: between the seventh day and the six days of work."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story moves on to the wording of the ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא's הבדלה text includes four distinctions.

steps.title: Isn't one distinction enough?
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב בר אבא asks why רבא said so much. רב taught that רבי יהודה הנשיא said only "between holy and ordinary."
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Why do you need all this? Didn't רב יהודה say in the name of רב: "Who separates between holy and ordinary" is the הבדלה of רבי יהודה הנשיא?
steps.whatsHappening: The guest challenges רבא's long wording. He cites a source that one short phrase is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a great authority like רבי יהודה הנשיא said only one distinction, the extra three seem unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't (so-and-so) say? (introduces a challenging source)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לְמָה לָךְ כּוּלֵּי הַאי?
phrases.english: He (Rav Yaakov bar Abba) said to him: Why do you need all this?
Didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Rav:
"Who separates between holy and ordinary"

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא הַבְדָּלָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא?
phrases.english: this is the havdala of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לָךְ כּוּלֵּי הַאי? וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording given in step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה הנשיא said only one distinction, so the extra ones are not needed.

steps.title: Say at least three distinctions and no more than seven
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that he follows רבי אושעיא: a person should say at least three distinctions and no more than seven. Then רב יעקב בר אבא begins to reply.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I hold like this teaching, which רבי אלעזר said in the name of רבי אושעיא: One who says fewer should not say fewer than three, and one who adds should not add more than seven. He said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his wording with a different source. This passage ends as the guest starts his next reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not follow the one-distinction view. He follows רבי אושעיא, who sets a minimum of three and a maximum of seven. His four distinctions fit within that range.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that there are two views on the wording of הבדלה: a single distinction, or a range of three to seven.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא כְּהָא סְבִירָא לִי,
phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him: I hold like this teaching,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: which Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Oshaya:
One who says fewer should not say fewer than three,
and one who adds should not add more than seven.
He (Rav Yaakov bar Abba) said to him:
phrases.notes: This opens the guest's next reply, which continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנָא כְּהָא סְבִירָא לִי, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One distinction is enough, as in רבי's הבדלה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא follows רבי אושעיא's range of three to seven, so four is correct.
